question_text: Acetamide on Hoffmann bromamide degradation (Br₂ and KOH) gives:
explanation: The amide loses its carbonyl carbon as carbonate, so the amine has one carbon less: CH₃CONH₂ → CH₃NH₂.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Which of the following is the strongest base in aqueous solution?
explanation: In water the order is (CH₃)₂NH > CH₃NH₂ > (CH₃)₃N > NH₃, from the balance of +I effect, hydration and steric hindrance.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Aniline is a weaker base than ammonia mainly because:

options.A: the lone pair on N is delocalised into the benzene ring
options.B: aniline has a higher molar mass
options.D: the benzene ring is electron-donating by +I effect

explanation: Resonance delocalises the nitrogen lone pair into the ring, so it is less available to accept a proton.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Which of the following gives a foul-smelling isocyanide in the carbylamine test (CHCl₃ and alcoholic KOH)?
explanation: Only primary amines (–NH₂) give the carbylamine test. The others are secondary or tertiary.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: The Hinsberg reagent is:
explanation: Benzenesulphonyl chloride (C₆H₅SO₂Cl) is used to distinguish primary, secondary and tertiary amines.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: The sulphonamide formed from a primary amine and benzenesulphonyl chloride dissolves in aqueous KOH because:

options.A: it has an acidic hydrogen on nitrogen
options.C: it has no hydrogen on nitrogen

explanation: The N–H hydrogen is made acidic by the strongly electron-withdrawing sulphonyl group, so the sulphonamide forms a soluble potassium salt.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Aniline reacts with NaNO₂ and HCl at 273–278 K to give:
explanation: This is diazotisation of a primary aromatic amine, which must be done at low temperature.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Benzenediazonium chloride on warming with water gives:
explanation: The diazonium group is replaced by OH with loss of N₂.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Benzenediazonium chloride on treatment with hypophosphorous acid (H₃PO₂) gives:
explanation: H₃PO₂ reduces the diazonium salt by replacing N₂⁺ with H.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Benzenediazonium chloride couples with phenol in alkaline medium to give:
explanation: The diazonium ion attacks the para position of the phenoxide ion, giving the orange azo dye p-hydroxyazobenzene.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Reduction of nitrobenzene with Zn and NH₄Cl (neutral medium) gives:
explanation: In neutral medium the reduction stops at the hydroxylamine stage. In acidic medium (Sn/HCl) it gives aniline.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is used to prepare:
explanation: Potassium phthalimide reacts with an alkyl halide, and hydrolysis gives the pure primary amine. Aryl halides do not undergo the required substitution.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Aniline reacts with bromine water at room temperature to give:
explanation: The –NH₂ group strongly activates the ring, so all three ortho and para positions are brominated and a white precipitate forms.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Direct nitration of aniline with HNO₃ and H₂SO₄ gives a substantial amount of m-nitroaniline because:

options.B: aniline is protonated to the anilinium ion, which is meta-directing
options.C: the nitro group enters through the nitrogen atom
options.D: sulphuric acid blocks the ortho and para positions

explanation: In strong acid –NH₂ becomes –NH₃⁺, which is deactivating and meta-directing.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Ethylamine on treatment with nitrous acid (NaNO₂ and HCl) gives:

options.B: ethyl diazonium chloride, stable at 273 K

explanation: Aliphatic diazonium salts are unstable and decompose at once to the alcohol with evolution of N₂.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Reduction of CH₃CN with LiAlH₄ gives:
explanation: R–C≡N is reduced to R–CH₂NH₂, so CH₃CN gives CH₃CH₂NH₂ with the same number of carbons.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Reduction of methyl isocyanide (CH₃NC) with H₂ and Ni gives:
explanation: R–N≡C is reduced to R–NH–CH₃, so CH₃NC gives the secondary amine (CH₃)₂NH.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Among the isomers of C₄H₁₁N, which has the highest boiling point?

options.D: all have the same boiling point

explanation: Primary amines have two N–H bonds and form the most intermolecular hydrogen bonds. Tertiary amines have none.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Which of the following is the weakest base?
explanation: The –NO₂ group withdraws electron density by –M and –I effects and makes the lone pair on N least available.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: The key intermediate in the Hoffmann bromamide degradation is:
explanation: The N-bromoamide rearranges to an isocyanate (R–N=C=O), which is hydrolysed to the amine with loss of CO₂.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Aniline reacts with acetyl chloride in the presence of pyridine to give:
explanation: This is N-acetylation, and pyridine removes the HCl formed.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: A secondary amine reacts with nitrous acid to give:
explanation: R₂NH + HNO₂ → R₂N–N=O + H₂O.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Which of the following reactions give primary amines?

options.D: Reduction of isocyanides with H₂ and Ni

explanation: Reduction of isocyanides gives secondary amines (R–NH–CH₃).
subject: Chemistry

question_text: Which statements about benzenediazonium chloride are correct?

options.A: It is stable only at about 273–278 K
options.B: It undergoes replacement reactions with loss of N₂
options.C: It undergoes coupling reactions with phenols and aromatic amines
options.D: It is stable at 300 K for several days

explanation: The salt decomposes on warming, so it is prepared and used cold.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: The number of isomeric amines (primary, secondary and tertiary) with the formula C₃H₉N is:
explanation: Propylamine, isopropylamine, ethylmethylamine and trimethylamine.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: The number of isomeric primary amines with the formula C₄H₁₁N is:
explanation: n-Butylamine, sec-butylamine, isobutylamine and tert-butylamine.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: The moles of N₂ released when 1 mole of ethylamine reacts completely with excess nitrous acid is:
explanation: C₂H₅NH₂ + HNO₂ → C₂H₅OH + N₂ + H₂O.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: The moles of Br₂ consumed by 1 mole of aniline in excess bromine water is:
explanation: Three bromine atoms are introduced at the two ortho and one para position, which gives 2,4,6-tribromoaniline.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: The number of carbon atoms in the amine formed from propanamide (CH₃CH₂CONH₂) by Hoffmann bromamide degradation is:
explanation: One carbon is lost, so the product is ethylamine, C₂H₅NH₂.
subject: Chemistry

question_text: The oxidation state of nitrogen in nitrobenzene is:
explanation: In the nitro group nitrogen is at +3 (as in nitrite), so the answer is +3.
subject: Chemistry
